name: Mursi
catalog_citation: Worku, Firew Girma. 2020. A grammar of Mursi, a Nilo-Saharan language. PhD thesis, James Cook University (researchonline.jcu.edu.au/65453).
catalog_locator: §2.6 Tone, pp. 98-99 (thesis pagination); also §1 overview p.~13 and §2.5.1.3 p. 59 (only 'stress' mentions)
catalog_quote: 2.6 Tone Mursi has two tone levels ― High (H] and Low (L). This contradicts what Turton and Bender suggested more than four decades ago. Turton and Bender (1976: 559) suggested that Mursi has four registered tones: high, mid, low, and falling. However, in this study, mid and falling tones are not attested. ... In Mursi, tone is important both lexically and grammatically. The syllable is the main tone-bearing unit in the language. A phonological word, whether it has anominal root or verbal root must have at least one syllable as a tone-bearing unit. Thus, it is the number of syllables carrying distinct tone levels which create different tonal melodies on nouns and verbs. That means that different tonal melodies will automatically generate tonal patterns depending on number of syllables in a word. ... Accordingly, depending on the number of syllables in a phonological word, nominal words …

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding passage (Worku 2020 section 2.6, pp. 98-99) and the domain quote (p. 13) are verbatim in the held text layer of the JCU thesis; the locator's two 'stress' mentions (p. 59 and fn. 7) are exactly as described and neither states a stress system. (2) Deciding source: a 2020 692-pp reference grammar (published by Brill 2021), the top item in Glottolog's list and the best available description; no instrumental or dedicated prosody study of Mursi exists (Glottolog's only 'phonology' item, Yigezu 2001 JIPA, is about Chai lip-plate articulation). (3) fetched sources now from mursi.org (open): the complete Turton & Bender 1976 sketch (our catalog copy was truncated and unread), Turton 1981 'Le Mun' (scanned), and the 2008 dictionary. sources.quote: '1.2. Ton et accent. Il est apparu difficile de dissocier ces deux phenomenes dans la structure de la phrase. ... des mots enregistres isolement ... peuvent etre groupes selon leurs schemes tonals particuliers; cependant, on n'a pas encore trouve ... de paires minimales ... on a indique l'accent en soulignant le segment accentue' (six tone signs: haut, moyen, bas, descendant, superieur, superieur descendant). Fn. on verbs: 'Dans la plupart d'entre eux, l'accent est sur la premiere syllabe du radical, mais dans ka-taka, ... il porte sur le prefixe.' Fn. p. 346: tones marked tentatively as heard
sources.locator: section 1.2 'Ton et accent', p. 335; fn. 1 p. 336 (verbs); fn. 1 p. 346 (specimen text)

sources.citation: Turton, David & M. Lionel Bender. 1976. Mursi. In M. L. Bender (ed.), The Non-Semitic Languages of Ethiopia, 533-561. East Lansing: African Studies Center, MSU. (mursi.org scan; complete download this time, catalog copy was truncated; the scan itself omits printed p. 539 and duplicates p. 540)
sources.quote: Nouns grouped by tone pattern (high-high, high-mid, mid-high, mid-mid, high or mid-falling, mid-low), then: 'There is reason to suspect that this analysis is inadequate. No noun is listed having initial low tone, and many of the 9 possible tone combinations ... are missing. A re-analysis with a larger sample is badly needed. Longer nouns (stress on first syllable): kabari "eye", kironoy "fly", hiranaha "woman", munini "star", liba kabari "seed", bakumu: mul "world", kulilo "claw". (Stress on second syllable): Ba:logi "leaf", Burui "egg", urgussi "fish", kirimogi "root".' I.e. impressionistic l

sources.quote: Describes 7 vowels, vowel length ('few contrastive examples'), 22 consonants, and a Latin orthography; no statement on tone or stress, and neither is marked in the orthography.
